title: Burst accounting stall on heterogeneous GPU clusters causing reserved pool shortfalls
creator: Evan Liu
description: Multiple customers on Dedicated pools reported sustained 502/429 errors and a rapid increase in request latency during burst windows. Investigation showed that the reserved-pool allocator intermittently stopped allocating burst slots for heterogeneous GPU clusters (mix of small and large GPU instance types). This produced effective capacity shortfalls for several tenants with burst traffic patterns and triggered escalations from two mid-market customers and one enterprise account.
steps_to_reproduce: Create a Dedicated reserved pool with mixed GPU flavors (A100-small, A100-large, T4) and enable burst credits for tenant X
Simulate bursty traffic using the load generator with short high TPS spikes for 2-3 minutes
Observe allocator logs and burst accounting: some burst requests remain queued despite available physical headroom on large instances
Reproduce alloc-decision trace to see normalized capacity values occasionally become 0 for some instance types

mitigation: Immediate mitigation was to flip the config flag to disallow packing across different GPU capacity classes in the autoscaler, which restored predictable allocation behavior for affected tenants. We also performed temporary manual capacity reservations for the three most impacted customers and applied increased alerting on allocator failure conditions.
root_cause: A bug in the allocator's normalizeCapacity routine used integer division when computing per-instance normalized weights. For heterogeneous fleets where one instance type has a smaller nominal slot size, truncation caused the algorithm to treat that type as contributing zero burst capacity under certain rounding edge cases. The scheduler then preferred other allocation vectors and eventually stalled due to a downstream fair-share threshold check that expected non-zero contributions, producing a deadlock-like stall in burst accounting.
fix_summary: Change normalization to use float arithmetic with robust rounding, add a minimum epsilon floor for per-instance contributions, and update the allocator to detect and reject invalid zero-weight vectors earlier. Add unit tests that exercise mixed small/large GPU fleets and a regression test that simulates the earlier truncation condition.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge PR to main with feature flag off. 2) Canary deploy to a small dedicated region (region-us-west-2) with synthetic burst generator for 24h. 3) Monitor allocator metrics (allocation_success_rate, zero_weight_count, queued_burst_requests) and customer traffic for regressions. 4) If stable, enable feature flag across remaining regions in 3-phase rollout over 48h. 5) After full rollout, re-enable heterogeneous packing with updated safety checks.
postmortem_actions: Add allocator telemetry metric 'normalized_weight_histogram' and alert when zero-weight buckets exceed threshold
Add a regression test in CI that replays the failing trace from the incident
Rework allocator docs to call out assumptions about heterogeneous fleet packing
Create a migration tool to rebalance tenants to homogeneous pools where clients want guaranteed burst behavior
Schedule a reliability spike to redesign the allocator packing heuristic to avoid single-point decision stalls
qa_and_tests: New unit tests for normalizeCapacity covering integer/float edge cases
Integration test that launches a mixed-GPU pool and runs the burst load generator
Chaos test to randomly flip feature flag and validate allocator recovers without losing existing reservations
longer_term_backlog: Investigate per-tenant smart bin-packing that accounts for GPU performance curves rather than nominal slot sizes
Explore allocator redesign to separate packing and fairness accounting stages to avoid coupling failures
Evaluate a tiered burst policy where critical customers get guaranteed homogeneous backing
communication_plan: Posted incident summary to affected customers with timeline and mitigations (internal link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/dedicated-incidents/ENG-1005001)
Status updates sent via support tickets and account manager threads
Draft blog/ops note for internal distro covering lessons learned and new telemetry
notes: This incident surfaced a lesser-tested code path that primarily impacts customers using mixed-instance Dedicated pools. The hotfix reduces packing efficiency temporarily but restores customer-facing reliability. We should prioritize the allocator redesign work in Q2 to regain efficiency without risking stall scenarios. The assignee will coordinate with Solutions Engineering to migrate affected tenants if they prefer a homogeneous pool during the rollback window.
